title: Learning trustworthy model from noisy labels based on rough set for surface defect detection
mechanism: Treat label noise as inconsistency on suspicious regions (rough-set boundary region), redesign the loss on those pixels and add a pluggable spatially correlated Bayesian module giving a defect-discrimination confidence.
adaptation: Define the boundary region as the 1-2 px ring around crack labels plus faint crack segments (7% are < 2% darker), apply the boundary loss there; use the confidence output for the benchmark's uncertainty column.
evidence: R: abstract claims effectiveness, robustness, real-time; numbers unverified (full text not read).
min_experiment: Arm: house with rough-set boundary loss on the ring + faint segments; baseline: house; metric: CV crack IoU and relF1@2; kill if IoU gain < +0.01. Read full text first.
prior_overlap: Partial: offset-tolerant CE (n.d.) is related; Bayesian confidence module untested.
